chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man in this era who had intercourse with his slave-girl, then doubted about her child. He wrote back: If there is resemblance in him [the child] from him [the master], then he is his child.
ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a child born to a slave-girl when the master doubts if he is the father?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahani's *al-Istibsar*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the application of *shabah* (resemblance) in cases of *shubha* (doubt) regarding a slave-girl's offspring, prioritizing physical likeness to the master as evidence of paternity. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving lineage disputes within the *ummah* system, ensuring the child's status and inheritance rights are determined by observable traits when explicit acknowledgment is absent. It reflects the practical legal reasoning employed by the Imams to address social complexities of their time.
